reason: Confirmed by reading the webview stack, not only the repo comment. downloadCsv uses a Blob plus <a download>. The app registers no on_download handler. On macOS, wry's WKWebView navigation delegate answers every shouldPerformDownload action with Cancel when no download handler exists, so both Export CSV buttons are silent no-ops on macOS: no throw, no toast. Windows WebView2 may use its default download UI; Windows is unverified.
evidence_checked: Read csv.ts and export-artifact.ts, grepped both callers, grepped src-tauri/src for on_download (none), then read the locked tauri 2.11.1, tauri-runtime-wry and wry 0.55.1 sources for default download behaviour. No GUI click (forbidden).
repro_check: grep -rn on_download src-tauri/src -> none; wry navigation.rs:68-74 -> should_download && !has_download_handler => WKNavigationActionPolicy::Cancel.

reason: The core claim holds: the product has no config, route or UI to add a user-chosen MCP server, and only openbb-mcp and sec-edgar-mcp are wired. Three corrections. (1) The 'universal tool layer' promise in the constitution and spec is MCP-as-SERVER, where one catalog is projected to external clients; nothing promises consuming user-added servers, so there is no positioning contradiction. (2) A generic stdio/http McpClient already exists (mcp_client.py:218), so the missing piece is only a config surface. (3) Most of the cited example servers are broker servers, which are now out of scope. Downgraded high -> medium.
evidence_checked: Grepped sidecar/ src/ src-tauri/src/ types/ plugins/ for MCP client and config surfaces. Only two hardcoded get_client callers exist; McpServerConfig has no consumer outside types/ and the keychain namespace. Read the constitution Principle II and spec US7 wording.
repro_check: grep -rn 'get_client(' sidecar --include=*.py -> only openbb-mcp and sec-edgar-mcp call sites; no route or UI takes an MCP server config.
